paper.title: Contrastive Identification and Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Develops contrastive identification and generation through common-crossing geometry, exact closure-dimension characterizations, clean and corrupted hierarchy separations, and defect-count robustness, while leaving finite-family geometry, effective algorithms, corrupted generation, and random presentations only partially or not formalized.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom twenty-seven-card surface has thirteen fully covered claim groups, eight partially covered groups, and six source claims or extensions with no Lean coverage. The strongest coverage is for the exact identification characterization, both closure-dimension theorems, defect identity, semantic co-singleton recovery, and corrupted incomparability; the full clean diamond, family-scale geometry, quantitative witness examples, constructive Algorithm 1, corrupted generation, and random presentations remain incomplete.
specializations: The paper observes unordered two-element sets, whereas Lean learners consume oriented Edge values. Crossing, incidence, and the dimension carrier are swap-invariant, but no target-scope theorem transports learners or proves prefix-level swap invariance.
Identification claims use indexed families while generation and geometry often use extensional Set (Set alpha) classes; concrete hierarchy and corruption witnesses are arithmetic families over Nat.
The semantic generators and identifiers use classical choice and do not establish computability, runtime, oracle complexity, convergence rates, or statistical guarantees.
Theorem 5.4's least-threshold wrapper compares only positive thresholds, resolving the empty-prefix dimension-zero boundary without changing the positive-round statement.
The repaired absenceCountIdentifier_finitely_identifies theorem directly names the budget-independent witness for Theorem 6.6, but fixed-enumeration tie-breaking and computability remain unproved.
gaps: The explicit N1/N2/N3 classification, Lemma 4.4 confusability corollary, and Lemma 4.6 strictness lack direct paper-shaped wrappers.
The full clean strict diamond is not packaged: CtrGen subset TxtGen and TxtId strict-subset TxtGen are absent at the target interface.
Proposition B.1, Proposition D.1, Example D.2, and the punctured family's unbounded hollow witnesses are source-only.
The printed Example 5.9 uses a false h-infinity versus h-m incomparability assertion and insufficient ambient assumptions; the appendix repairs the result but Lean uses a different punctured witness.
The overview's general pairwise-infinite-defect implication to finite-corruption identification is neither a numbered source theorem nor a Lean theorem.
Algorithm 1 lacks fixed-enumeration tie-breaking, computability, oracle-free execution, and runtime certification; Example 6.7 lacks its extension asymptotic wrapper.
Corrupted contrastive generation, random presentations, almost-sure coverage, phase transitions, spectral methods, and rates have no Lean interface.

audit_refs.scope: Checksum-pinned arXiv-v1 AI-assisted statement-faithfulness audit plus separately tracked named-witness repair chronology. It did not inspect proof bodies or provide human certification.
The authoritative ledger keeps P28 human correspondence pending; the named-witness repair is kernel-checked separately.

Project axiom checks cover the principal P28 theorems. A temporary draft audit additionally resolved all forty-four proposed endpoints, defining modules, and allowed logical dependencies; neither check establishes source correspondence.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Twenty-seven claim groups: Definition 4.1 with Proposition 4.2; Theorem 4.3; Lemmas 4.4 and 4.6; Definition 4.5 with Theorem 4.7 and Remark 4.8; Definitions 5.1--5.3; Theorems 5.4--5.5; Example 5.7; Proposition 5.8; Example 5.9; Definition 5.10 with Proposition 5.11; Proposition B.1; Proposition 5.12; Theorems 5.13--5.14; Proposition D.1 with Example D.2; Definition 6.1; Definition 6.2 with Proposition 6.3; the overview-level infinite-defect principle; Definition 6.4 with Theorem 6.5; Algorithm 1; Theorem 6.6; Example 6.7; Theorem 6.8; Definition E.1 with Remark E.2; and Definition E.3 with its statistical claims.
exclusions: Section 3's Angluin, informant-identification, ordinary text-generation, and presentation results are imported background rather than P28 primary claims. The missing Theorem 3.7 target bridge is recorded as a Theorem 5.13 component instead of duplicated.

Appendices A and C proof-only steps, subordinate interface definitions, low-level finite-set and stream bookkeeping, and implementation helpers are excluded when a canonical paper-facing wrapper is linked.

Abstract and conclusion paraphrases are folded into precise cards. The unsupported general infinite-defect principle is retained separately because it materially exceeds Proposition 6.3 and the co-singleton instance.
Open questions about robust closure dimension and broader effective procedures are folded into the Definition E.1 and Algorithm 1 cards rather than receiving additional conjecture cards.
Related work and editorial exposition do not receive standalone cards.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for this twenty-seven-card custom scope, not for every numbered background statement or proof step. Page locators are printed pages of the checksum-pinned 23-page arXiv-v1 author PDF.
